description: The figure is a single, axis-free composition table rendered as an image (no micrograph, curve or schematic panels). Its header row reads "Element", "Mn" and "Al". Two data rows report the measured composition of the two phases: "In ferrite (wt.%)" with Mn 10.3 ± 0.1 and Al 6.0 ± 0.1, and "In Austenite (wt.%)" with Mn 12.8 ± 0.1 and Al 4.7 ± 0.1. Every tabulated value carries an uncertainty of ±0.1 wt.%; no Fe balance, no other elements and no processing rows are listed. Read directly from the table, Mn is higher in austenite than in ferrite, whereas Al is higher in ferrite than in austenite — i.e. the two solutes partition in opposite directions between the phases. The caption states that the table gives the chemical composition of the experimented steel after deformation at 500 °C at 0.001 s⁻¹ up to a true strain of 0.6, obtained from SEM analysis. The table therefore supplies the chemical-partitioning evidence for the paper's argument that warm deformation drives a bi-directional ferrite-to-austenite transformation with strain-induced redistribution of Mn and Al between ferrite and austenite.

subfigures.description: Two-column composition table with header cells "Element", "Mn", "Al" and two data rows, "In ferrite (wt.%)" (Mn 10.3 ± 0.1, Al 6.0 ± 0.1) and "In Austenite (wt.%)" (Mn 12.8 ± 0.1, Al 4.7 ± 0.1). No other rows or columns are present.

observations.observation: The figure consists of a single tabular data block whose header row is "Element", "Mn", "Al".
Row "In ferrite (wt.%)" lists Mn = 10.3 ± 0.1 and Al = 6.0 ± 0.1.
Row "In Austenite (wt.%)" lists Mn = 12.8 ± 0.1 and Al = 4.7 ± 0.1.
Mn content is higher in austenite (12.8 wt.%) than in ferrite (10.3 wt.%), so Mn partitions to austenite.
Al content is higher in ferrite (6.0 wt.%) than in austenite (4.7 wt.%), so Al partitions to ferrite.
All four tabulated values are given with the same uncertainty, ±0.1 wt.%.
Only Mn and Al are tabulated; no Fe balance and no other element contents appear in the table.
The caption states the compositions were obtained from SEM analysis of the experimented steel.
The caption states the steel was deformed at 500 °C at 0.001 s⁻¹ up to a true strain of 0.6.

The caption titles this content "Chemical composition of experimented steel after deformation", i.e. the table reports post-deformation, phase-specific composition rather than the nominal alloy composition.
The table is form-consistent with a phase-partitioning measurement: the same two elements are reported for both the ferrite and the austenite phase after the same deformation condition.
